# dsh-session-takeout
**English** · 简体中文

Packs one DeepSeek Harness conversation into a single ZIP, so you can carry it to
another computer a
nd keep talking there.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Below the message box there are two small buttons:

- **导出会话 / Export session** — packs the current conversation into one ZIP in
`~/Downloads`, then rev

eals it in Finder.
- **导入会话包 / Import bundle** — restores such a ZIP on this computer, opens it, and
continues the conversation.
## Why the Host does the work

A conversation is not just text in the browser. The durable event log, the attachment
object store a

nd the workspace registry live on the machine running the Host, so the
Client half only presses two

workspace registry live on the machine running the Host, so the
Client half only presses two routes:
| Route | Purpose |

| `POST /session-takeout/export` | `{ sessionId }` → writes and reveals a ZIP, returns its path |
|

`POST /session-takeout/import` | raw ZIP bytes → restores the session, returns its new id |
| `POST
/session-takeout/reveal` | `{ path }` → reveals a path in Finder |
## What is inside a bundle
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The container is an ordinary ZIP (deflate, UTF-8 names, no ZIP64), written with
`node:zlib` and a lo

cal CRC-32 table so no dependency is pulled in. It opens in Finder,
Explorer and `unzip`; the conver
sation itself stays readable without this plugin.

The `format` tag inside `manifest.json` stays `dsh-session-bundle` on purpose: the
archive format is

versioned separately from the project name, so bundles written by
earlier builds keep importing aft

eparately from the project name, so bundles written by
earlier builds keep importing after a rename.
## Export is durable, import is careful

- **Export** first flushes the live session through the sessions service, because a
conversation tha

t is still being written would otherwise be short of events. It then
reads the durable log and copie

s only attachments the events actually reference.
- **Import** never touches this machine's store un

til the archive has been fully parsed
and every entry CRC-verified. It then:
- restores attachments

into the content-addressed object store (existing objects win),
- writes the log under the *local* s

ession format version,
- points the restored session's `cwd` at a fresh directory,
- mints a new ses

sion id when the source id already exists here,
- registers that directory as a workspace and attach
es the session to it.

A restored conversation therefore lands in
`~/Documents/DeepSeek Harness/<title>-<shortid>/`, which

becomes its workspace — the
exporter's absolute paths are never reused.
## Carrying it to a computer that has never seen this plugin

Every exported ZIP carries this plugin's sources under `plugin/`, so a fresh machine
needs nothing b

ZIP carries this plugin's sources under `plugin/`, so a fresh machine
needs nothing but the archive:

1. Copy the ZIP over and unzip it.
2. Install `plugin/` as a bundle (`plugin_manager → install_bundl

e → <unzipped>/plugin`).
On a machine that has never run this plugin, ask its agent to do this step

— it can
also post the ZIP to the route itself, without opening any dialog:
`curl -X POST http://127

.0.0.1:<port>/session-takeout/import --data-binary @bundle.zip`
3. Click **导入会话包 / Import bundle** a

nd pick the ZIP (or let the agent's request do
the same thing), then the restored conversation opens

let the agent's request do
the same thing), then the restored conversation opens ready to continue.
## Limits worth knowing

- Attachments whose object file is missing on the exporting machine are listed in
`manifest.json` un

der `missingAttachments` and simply do not travel.
- A session that was forked from another conversa

tion keeps its `inheritedEventCount`;
the parent's prefix is not part of the bundle, so only the par

t stored in this log
arrives.
- `agentPreset` travels as an id. If that preset is not installed on t

he target, the
session opens with the default agent.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The bundle patch inserts one row; nothing else in the profile needs editing. Restart
the Web UI (or

let the client plugin hot-reload) and the two buttons appear under the
message box.
